base_method_text.title:
Characteristic Guidance: Non-linear Correction for Diffusion Model at
  Large Guidance Scale
base_method_text.summary:
Popular guidance for denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) linearly
combines distinct conditional models together to provide enhanced control over
samples. However, this approach overlooks nonlinear effects that become
significant when guidance scale is large. To address this issue, we propose
characteristic guidance, a guidance method that provides first-principle
non-linear correction for classifier-free guidance. Such correction forces the
guided DDPMs to respect the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation of diffusion process,
in a way that is training-free and compatible with existing sampling methods.
Experiments show that characteristic guidance enhances semantic characteristics
of prompts and mitigate irregularities in image generation, proving effective
in diverse applications ranging from simulating magnet phase transitions to
latent space sampling.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper addresses the issue of non-linearity in classifier-free guidance for denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) at large guidance scales. It introduces "characteristic guidance," a training-free method that provides non-linear correction by adhering to the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation, enhancing semantic characteristics and mitigating irregularities in image generation.
base_method_text.methodology: The proposed characteristic guidance method involves a non-linear correction term (∆x) applied to classifier-free guidance. This correction is determined by solving a fixed-point equation derived from the score Fokker-Planck equation using the method of characteristics and a harmonic ansatz. Orthogonal projection operators are used as regularization to accelerate computation.
base_method_text.experimental_setup: Experiments were conducted on conditional Gaussian distributions, mixtures of Gaussian distributions, CIFAR-10, ImageNet 256, and Stable Diffusion. Metrics used include Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), negative log-likelihood (NLL), and visual inspection.
base_method_text.limitations: The effectiveness of FID as an evaluation metric for guided DDPMs is questioned due to its focus on marginal probabilities rather than conditional probabilities. The iterative computation required for the non-linear correction can be slow without effective regularization.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring advanced regularization techniques beyond projection to enhance the convergence rate and accelerate computation. Additionally, the paper suggests the need for more appropriate metrics that address the discrepancy between target conditional probabilities and marginal probabilities for evaluating guided DDPMs.

add_method_texts.title: FiT: Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion Model
add_method_texts.summary:
Nature is infinitely resolution-free. In the context of this reality,
existing diffusion models, such as Diffusion Transformers, often face
challenges when processing image resolutions outside of their trained domain.
To overcome this limitation, we present the Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT),
a transformer architecture specifically designed for generating images with
unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios. Unlike traditional methods that
perceive images as static-resolution grids, FiT conceptualizes images as
sequences of dynamically-sized tokens. This perspective enables a flexible
training strategy that effortlessly adapts to diverse aspect ratios during both
training and inference phases, thus promoting resolution generalization and
eliminating biases induced by image cropping. Enhanced by a meticulously
adjusted network structure and the integration of training-free extrapolation
techniques, FiT exhibits remarkable flexibility in resolution extrapolation
generation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the exceptional performance
of FiT across a broad range of resolutions, showcasing its effectiveness both
within and beyond its training resolution distribution. Repository available at
https://github.com/whlzy/FiT.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT), a novel transformer architecture for diffusion models, enabling image generation at arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios. Key contributions include a flexible training pipeline eliminating cropping, a unique transformer architecture for dynamic token length modeling, and a training-free resolution extrapolation method.
add_method_texts.methodology: FiT models images as sequences of dynamically-sized tokens, using a flexible training pipeline that preserves original aspect ratios. The architecture incorporates 2D Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE), Swish-Gated Linear Unit (SwiGLU), and Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA). Training-free resolution extrapolation techniques, VisionNTK and VisionYaRN, are adapted for 2D RoPE.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The models were trained on the ImageNet dataset with a maximum token length of 256. Evaluation metrics include Fre'chet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. Experiments were conducted on various resolutions and aspect ratios, both within and outside the training distribution.
add_method_texts.limitations: The FiT-XL/2 model was only trained for 1.8 million steps, leading to slightly inferior performance at 256x256 resolution compared to DiT-XL/2. The generative capabilities with higher resolution training and exploration of resolution extrapolation methods requiring additional training were not thoroughly investigated.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring FiT's generative capabilities when trained with higher resolutions and larger token length limits, as well as delving into resolution extrapolation methods that require additional training.

new_method:
Below is the outcome of step 3—a genuinely new method that fuses core ideas from the Base Method (Characteristic Guidance) and a selected approach from the Add Method (FiT-style flexible tokenization). This new approach addresses one of the Base Method’s critical issues—namely, its limited adaptability to varying resolutions and aspect ratios—while retaining its non-linear Fokker-Planck–inspired corrections.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3) NEW METHOD PROPOSAL
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
We propose “Multi-Scale Characteristic Guidance with Dynamic Tokenization” (MCG-DT), a two-stage procedure that integrates dynamic token sequences for various resolutions into the characteristic guidance framework. This new method goes beyond a simple partial modification by introducing a multi-resolution sampling pipeline, harmonizing characteristic guidance with flexible spatial layouts:

1. Dynamic Tokenization & Multi-Resolution Blocks:  
   • Unlike the Base Method’s single-resolution approach, MCG-DT applies a FiT-like encoding, where images (or latent features) are partitioned into variable-length token sequences. Each token block represents an adaptive visual patch, allowing for an unbounded range of resolutions and aspect ratios.  
   • During sampling, MCG-DT processes tokens at multiple resolutions in a coarse-to-fine manner, incrementally refining the denoised image features.  

2. Hierarchical Characteristic Guidance:  
   • We retain the Base Method’s first-principle non-linear correction derived from the Fokker-Planck equation but distribute it hierarchically across different token scales.  
   • A project-and-correct cycle is performed at each resolution block: the characteristic guidance correction enforces the FP consistency condition, and an orthogonal projection regularizes the token corrections for computational efficiency.  

3. Cooperative Corrections Across Scales:  
   • Token-level intermediate representations at a coarser resolution guide the next resolution’s characteristic correction. This “preview” step provides alignment cues for the next token set, preserving coherent global structure while still enabling detail enhancement at finer scales.  
   • By propagating the non-linear corrections across multiple resolutions, MCG-DT both upholds semantic fidelity (as intended by characteristic guidance) and handles out-of-distribution resolutions effectively (benefiting from FiT’s token-based strategy).  

4. Training-Free Resolution Extrapolation:
   • As in FiT, MCG-DT uses training-free extrapolation mechanisms (e.g., adaptation of RoPE or attention masks to handle changing token lengths) so that the model can gracefully switch to higher or non-square resolutions. The hierarchical characteristic guidance then ensures that these extrapolations still respect the FP-equation–based corrections.  

Overall, MCG-DT tackles the Base Method’s challenge of fixed-size processing and computational inefficiency for out-of-distribution image dimensions, merging the flexible token modeling of FiT and the non-linear FP-driven corrections of characteristic guidance into a cohesive, multi-scale pipeline. This approach greatly broadens the applicability of characteristic guidance while preserving its robust semantic control.
